answer: Verifiable delay functions resist sybils: each identity computes a strictly sequential proof anchored to the unpredictable epoch beacon, taking fixed wall-clock time that parallel hardware cannot shorten. Since extra cores give no speedup, one machine sustains only one proof per window, so N live identities need N machines running real time. The beacon anchor blocks precomputation; the proof is a jade token, cheap to check, costly to forge. Sequential time is the bridge a swarm cannot widen.
